attack_name: LATS — 'Break Me If You Can' (multi-turn attacker-LLM-free lexical-anchor tree search)
summary: Multi-turn, black-box, attacker-LLM-free jailbreak. The victim T is made to generate its own pool of benign/harmful prompt-completion pairs; LATS then steers T toward the goal P* over a few turns by injecting only the missing content words ('lexical anchors'), never restating the full malicious request. BFS over Completion-Expansion / Anchor-Injection nodes; first judge 'yes' halts (shortest trajectory).

payload_contract.signal: live target output + HarmBench yes/no judge verdict per node
payload_contract.feedback_dependency: adaptive — each node's expansion query and BFS halt depend on live target output + judge; no fixed replayable artifact

data.dataset: AdvBench (Zou et al. 2023, 520 goals, vendored verbatim)
data.regenerate: N/A — shipped in full; run a --sample-rows slice

metrics.paper_reported_asr: 91.2% avg AdvBench across 9 SOTA models (Sec 6.1); 92.3% HarmBench; 100% on GPT-4o/Vicuna-13B/Mistral-7B

substitutions: No official code release; reimplemented from Algorithm 1 + verbatim appendix prompts (Appendix 12/13/14).

Single-LLM HarmBench yes/no judge substituted for the paper's Llama-3.3-8B/70B + GPT-4o-mini majority-vote ensemble; open-model victim (DeepSeek-v4-flash) substituted for GPT-5.1/GPT-4o etc. (model_substitution_run).
This run used the deterministic lexical fallback (sentence-transformers/spaCy unavailable); tagged embedder_backend/anchor_backend in run JSON.
